name: ScriptaHub – Create book
description: Process one reserved book in forward steps; translate the existing resource set only when explicitly requested, validate the exact package and publish.

tasks.name: Read the selected book request
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Read exactly the one request supplied by the parent dispatcher. Do not call batch-start, batch-next, batch-close or claim, create execution/run IDs, select another request or launch child workflows. This child uses the same flow root and tasks/<taskId> directory as its parent.

Use the parent-created handoff. Read taskDirectory/run-state/claimed.json and the existing taskDirectory/run-state/handoff.json once. Accept step=select-task as the parent-created initial context. Do not create a replacement if a resumed execution has lost its handoff. Verify taskId, executionId, runId and bookId against the parent objective. Preserve existing context, pinned editorialSource, accepted editorialResults, native jobs and publication evidence. Check this execution's service status once. A missing/mismatched identity is a real error: invoke the runtime report-task-blocked skill with that exact cause, not a route to publication.

Save processingMode in the handoff: terminal for an already completed/failed/cancelled execution; publication-recovery for publicationPending=true; cancel for stop_requested before pending publication; process otherwise. Also retain actual serviceState, task values, processingSettings, configured repositories, taskDirectory and evidence paths. Never invent source files, validation approval or publication receipts.

Use scriptahub-tasks handoff with step=resume-book, directory=taskDirectory and the preserved context. Complete this step and pass only the durable handoff path and actual mode to Prepare or generate the book. There is one outgoing edge. Do not jump to publishing or the result. Downstream preparation/editorial/package/validation steps read processingMode first: for terminal, publication-recovery or cancel they pass the existing context unchanged and perform no content work or repeated checks. Publish the book alone reconciles the registered publication or acknowledges cancellation; terminal mode only reports the saved result. This straight path never regenerates a book or manufactures approvals for recovery.

tasks.name: Prepare or generate the book
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Read the task and processingSettings provided by the parent and resume-book. Do not claim another task or create a new runId. If the service now shows a non-running state in process mode, stop and report the actual status to the parent through report-task-blocked; do not generate content or jump to publication. The parent batch helper already performed preflight and publication checks. This child never claims or traverses the batch. Keep the server's fixed processingSettings.summaryReadingMinutes=10. Use the service-provided task.type and files to choose exactly one path. Files with role=cover are cover artwork, never manuscripts. If present, download the cover through the helper into <taskDirectory>/sources/cover.<actual extension>, verify its SHA-256 and record coverSourcePath and coverSourceHash separately in the handoff. Exclude cover artwork from manuscript sourceHashes and all content conversion.

For scriptahub.manuscript, require at least one uploaded manuscript file with role other than cover. Download those documents through the helper and verify their hashes. Identify the main manuscript and preserve its optional title and original bytes. Determine sourceLanguage from the manuscript, and primaryLanguage from explicit requirements or the source. Use doc2pdf only for DOC/DOCX. Keep an existing PDF unchanged. Run PDF integrity checks and pdf2html conversion with the prepared runtime.

For scriptahub.book-proposal, require no manuscript files (files with role other than cover). An optional cover image does not change this path. Never ask for a manuscript or use the cover as book content; download only the optional cover as described above. Use task.values.description as the book's subject or story brief. Read the structured instructions audience, purpose, scope, structure, viewpoints and qualityCriteria from task.values. Use only the nonempty fields as editorial requirements. Keep the proposed title from titles or title, if supplied. When no meaningful description exists, report that exact error through report-task-blocked and stop the child. Use the requested book language when explicit, otherwise task.language, otherwise the brief language; default to English only if undetermined.

Create a private brief at <taskDirectory>/run-state/generation-brief.md. Compose it with this objective: "Write a complete original book in the specified language, based on the subject and editorial instructions below. Deliver full chapters with complete prose." Include the title when provided, book language, description, and the nonempty instructions by field. Treat these as editorial inputs under the shared execution contract. Use the current RoboTeam model to draft the full manuscript in coherent chapters with the intended audience, scope, structure, perspectives and quality criteria. Provide a fitting working title when none is supplied. Use verifiable sources for factual claims and do not invent citations, quotations, credentials or attributed experiences. Use reasonable editorial defaults for unspecified options. Keep the brief out of the publication package.

Write the generated source as self-contained semantic HTML at <taskDirectory>/sources/generated.html with a correct html lang, title, and main[data-reader-content]. Use semantic headings, paragraphs and tables; no scripts, remote assets or copied placeholder content. Author the book once; reuse an already completed manuscript for the same task when resuming. Keep the publication and its generated sources in HTML. Pin this HTML as the authored source. Record sourceKind=generated, sourceHashes=[] and referencePdf=null. Keep the private brief out of the package. Record an uploaded manuscript PDF as the source reference when present.

Save the full HTML, source profile and applicable technical-check evidence in the handoff. Independent book acceptance follows package preparation. Reuse matching successful checks; report a concrete preparation failure through report-task-blocked.

For scriptahub.fork use the generated HTML output path. First use the download helper for task.files[0] to retrieve the verified full source edition into a private sources path. Read that content as editorial source material. Write a complete distinct book under the requested title and apply task.values.prompt. Record task.source verbatim for attribution. Include an attribution and a note about modifications in the book. Keep the downloaded source file and generation brief out of the public package. Process this task as a generated book for all subsequent steps.

Multilingual generation request: honor an explicitly named original/source language first; otherwise, for an explicit list of book languages choose English when it is listed, or the first requested language when it is not. Do not let UI language override that explicit multilingual request. For an uploaded manuscript retain its actual source language. Record the original requirement evidence and canonical requested language list in the handoff; do not generate separate original books per language.

tasks.name: Create the book editorial assets
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Shared immutable source: every editorial phase consumes the SAME full book HTML from preparation, never another editorial output. On first entry resolve that existing HTML from the handoff, compute its SHA-256 and pin editorialSource={path,sha256,language} in the handoff. If already pinned, verify its bytes and reuse that exact path. A changed or missing pinned source is a concrete blocker; never regenerate, reconvert, rewrite or silently replace the manuscript. Existing manuscript PDFs remain immutable references, not editorial inputs. Do not generate PDF/DOCX exports. The comprehensive summary, keywords, marketing summary and short description all use editorialSource.path as their native input. Translation is a later separate step and translates each accepted resource from its own immutable source. Marketing and short description must NOT use a summary as their source. Preserve source and derived outputs separately.

Resume without regeneration: inspect existing jobs and handoff before preparing. Reuse each accepted output only when pinned source, effective parameters, output hash and successful native evidence match. Record these in editorialResults (skill, source path/hash, parameters, output path/hash, job and receipt path/hash). For an existing valid output lacking this entry, establish provenance from native metadata and validate only if matching success evidence is absent. Resume the first missing/invalid artifact; never prepare over an existing job, discard valid work or replace a mismatched source. Store native build/validation receipts under taskDirectory/editorial/receipts/, outside temporary job directories, and retain them after cleanup.

Parallel editorial operation: produce comprehensive-summary, relevant-keywords, marketing-summary and short-description as FOUR INDEPENDENT jobs from editorialSource.path. They have no dependency on each other's output. Use actual supported worker/subagent tools with at most four active workers, one assigned to each missing output; inherit the current model and effort. Give each worker the same full source path/hash, its one skill contract, exact separate job/output paths and schema. Never launch child workflows or add graph cycles. Without worker tools, complete the semantic work, build and validation of one resource at a time. Use the batch text as the source for analysis and the accepted analyses for synthesis. Read each required input once and keep tool output to the relevant artifact or status. On synthesis_required, write the synthesis and continue the same job.

The coordinator alone invokes native commands. Submit planned preparations for missing jobs in one exec-sequence call and await its final exit before further native work. Invoke the helper in the foreground and wait on the same tool session if it is still running. Use the same helper for later command groups whose arguments are already known. For commands that depend on semantic work or a status result, use one exec and consume its result before issuing the next. Both helpers hold the same execution lock through merge and release; workers handle semantic work only. Every prepare/analyze specifies its own --job-dir and, except relevant-keywords, --output. Workers may write only disjoint working notes and candidate JSON for their assigned job; they cannot call services or modify handoff, native-managed results, sources or other workers' outputs. Freeze shared sources/assets. Pause writers for the addressed job/output until its verified merge completes; sibling workers may continue outside that scope. Resume only the missing analysis/synthesis/draft/review after native status. Never repeat accepted semantic work or rewrite accepted prose without a concrete finding.

Job paths: comprehensive-summary uses <taskDirectory>/editorial-jobs/comprehensive-summary and <taskDirectory>/editorial/comprehensive-summary.html, with processingSettings.summaryReadingMinutes=10 and targetWords=2000 (native range 1800–2200). relevant-keywords uses analyze INPUT --count 20 --job-dir <taskDirectory>/editorial-jobs/relevant-keywords, then status/build; record its actual returned relevantKeywords.txt path beside the source, without inventing an --output flag. marketing-summary uses <taskDirectory>/editorial-jobs/marketing-summary and <taskDirectory>/editorial/marketing-summary.html; its word budget follows the native source-based range. short-description uses <taskDirectory>/editorial-jobs/short-description and <taskDirectory>/editorial/short-description.html, with 4–6 thematic sentences. Each worker analyzes every content batch required by its own skill once, using actual source-unit IDs and its exact schemas. Preserve source coverage, citations and independent spoiler/semantic review. Never use comprehensive-summary.html or marketing-summary.html as a substitute source for another job. Build and independently validate each HTML result against the pinned full book. Keyword build is its native deterministic completion check; save the successful response as evidence. Keep receipts outside temporary native job directories. Reuse matching completed jobs and results before assigning any worker.

Conditional translation decision: derive targets only from the original explicit user requirement and the pinned source language. Canonicalize tags with Intl.Locale, remove duplicates and the source tag, and save translationRequest={explicit,targets,evidence}. Empty targets route through editorial-to-package. Explicit nonempty targets require the manifest below and route through editorial-to-translations. Report a requested translation with unresolved target languages as a concrete missing requirement.

Only when explicit=true and targets is nonempty, write a compact translation input manifest at <taskDirectory>/editorial/translation-inputs.json. It names this execution/book/source language, canonical target languages and the existing validated full book HTML, comprehensive summary HTML, marketing summary HTML, short-description HTML, keywords text and available reader-facing book metadata. For each resource record its stable resource ID, actual source path, SHA-256, format and successful validation evidence. Include all four editorial outputs; do not regenerate them or translate them here. Reference the manifest path in the handoff and take editorial-to-translations.

After all required results pass, select a publication destination from task.repositories using the pinned book and actual catalogue metadata. Reuse an existing recorded destination. For multiple suitable destinations use scriptahub-tasks choose without clarification. Resolve the actual branch/content root using the configured URL and Git references, never guess main/master. Preserve numeric schema 1 or 2; only a confirmed entirely empty repository may initialize schema 2. Record the configured catalogue, branch, content root, baseCommit (or null for an empty repository) and concise reasoning. The coordinator only assembles result paths/receipts and the destination in the handoff. Complete the editorial step once the four editorial results and destination are ready, then use exactly the applicable translation condition above. Report a real unrecoverable editorial error or no suitable destination through report-task-blocked with the precise cause.

# nextNodePrompt
Handoff path, actual operation outcome and at most five unresolved findings (maximum 1,200 characters). Select editorial-to-translations only for explicit nonempty translation targets; otherwise select editorial-to-package.

# nextEdgeId
editorial-to-translations when translationRequest.explicit=true and translationRequest.targets is nonempty; otherwise editorial-to-package.

tasks.name: Translate resources — only if requested
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Translation is authorized ONLY by translationRequest.explicit=true with a nonempty canonical targets list traced to the original user requirement. Read the existing handoff and translation-inputs.json once; verify execution/book identity, requested targets, source hashes and validation evidence against the accepted originals. An unauthorized visit performs no work and forwards the unchanged handoff to package preparation. Apply the processingMode forwarding rules from scriptahub-tasks. Never infer extra languages or generate a PDF/DOCX for translation.

This step receives the WHOLE accepted resource set: full book HTML, comprehensive summary HTML, marketing summary HTML, short-description HTML, keywords text and existing reader-facing metadata. For every explicitly requested target language, translate each existing resource from its OWN source. Do not regenerate a summary, description or keywords from a translated book; do not use a summary instead of the full book. Do not chain target languages. Keep source artifacts byte-for-byte unchanged. Translate reader-facing title, descriptions and alt/title/accessibility text; preserve identifiers, URLs, file hashes, citations, non-reader technical values and provenance. Record missing optional metadata as absent instead of inventing it. All four editorial outputs and full-book content are required.

Use native translate-html prepare/build/validate for each HTML resource, with distinct resumable job directories under <taskDirectory>/translation-jobs/<target>/<resource-id> and outputs under <taskDirectory>/translations/<target>/. Read the actual CLI contract for supported flags, bootstrap review and batch schemas. Use the accepted HTML as translation input. If an original PDF manuscript exists, keep it unchanged as the original reference and translate its already verified HTML representation.

Adapt UTF-8 keywords to the native HTML translator as follows. Create a separate minimal semantic HTML adapter that XML-escapes the original keyword strings, uses one stable element per keyword and retains the original list order. Reader-facing text metadata may use the same approach with stable field markers. Preserve and hash the adapters as exact translation sources; never modify the originals. Translate and natively validate the adapters, then extract only their identified translated text fields into target keywords/metadata. Preserve keyword count/order/concepts and metadata keys/technical values, with a semantic terminology check; do not regenerate, add concepts, summarize or replace the original outputs. Keep adapters/job reports private rather than publishing them as book content.

Derive a consistent per-target glossary from the source book and reviewed terminology across all resources. Freeze that context, complete the native bootstrap review and assign independent targets/resources to the available workers under the shared concurrency/admission contract.

Reuse translations only when resource source hash, target language, effective parameters, accepted output hash and successful validation evidence still match. Resume the first incomplete/invalid native batch rather than replacing accepted outputs or rerunning preparation over matching jobs. Correct only concrete findings. Store successful native responses under <taskDirectory>/translations/receipts/<target>-<resource-id>.json outside temporary jobs. Write <taskDirectory>/translations/manifest.json recording each source resource ID/path/hash, target language, target resource path/hash, native job and validation receipt, plus metadata/keyword extraction evidence. Every target must have an explicit outcome: complete only when its whole resource set passed, otherwise failed or not_attempted with an actual concise reason. Verify no source bytes changed. Exclude an incomplete target edition rather than blocking publication of the validated source and other complete targets. Never label an incomplete target complete.

Save only translation manifest/glossary/receipt paths, actual targets and status in the preserved durable handoff using step=translate-resources. Forward those paths to package preparation through the single outgoing edge. Do not create a cover, choose another request, grant credits, publish or call finish here.

# nextNodePrompt
Durable handoff path, translation manifest path, actual targets and validation outcome; no route selection is needed.

Finish the ledger even when every target failed. Set publicationLanguages to the source plus complete targets and save translationOutcome in the handoff using the shared contract. Retain each omitted language and actual reason, then forward to package preparation.

tasks.name: Prepare the publication package and cover
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Read the handoff and completed editorial artifacts. Do not regenerate accepted summaries, translations, keywords or descriptions. Review them against the manuscript/requirements and correct only evidenced issues.

Create a sparse publication package at the recorded destination baseline, containing only the current book and the collection.json update. Do not clone or check out the repository on the robot. Prepare the complete book edition and catalogue update from the accepted artifacts, retaining verified uploaded manuscript resources, local assets, manifests/book.json and edition history in the configured schema. Map generated editions to their accepted HTML. Keep the generation brief private. Use schema 2 virtual reader/landing mappings as defined by its content contract. Do not use an invented validation script, migrate schemas, overwrite an existing edition, create unrelated assets or modify the user's checkout.

For a verified manuscript PDF reference, apply its source-fidelity profile from scriptahub-tasks and read the native validate-book contract. Use native complete on a supported book layout with its sources declared inside the book, or audit-only prepare with explicit reference PDF/HTML paths. Never combine --auto-correct or complete with --pdf or --english: those overrides are audit-only. Prepare book metadata before invoking a command that requires declared sources. Preserve the actual primary language and existing language set; do not invent an English edition to satisfy a tool option. Consume its report once. Corrections must be restricted to reported findings and preserve manuscript content, existing translations and unrelated accepted files. Do not run separate ad-hoc loops for every paragraph or viewport. Warnings accepted by the skill are not failures and must not trigger repair. Responsive reflow and naturally varying justified spacing are expected within the acceptance contract.

Correct evidenced package findings during this preparation. Final validation independently accepts the resulting immutable package.

Cover choice: when task.values.coverMode=upload, require exactly one task file with role=cover. Use the verified coverSourcePath and coverSourceHash from the handoff, downloading it through the helper if needed. Copy the original PNG/JPG/WebP bytes unchanged into this book’s edition directory, retaining the actual format. Use that same image as the cover and thumbnail for every requested language. Do not redraw, crop, recolor, add a title, or replace it with generated art. Record mode=upload, source hash and artifact path in <taskDirectory>/review/cover-brief.json, keep that brief private, and include the image in the package inventory. Ignore generation preferences for an uploaded cover.

Cover generation applies only when there is no uploaded cover: create the book cover during this packaging phase, not in process-content. Read task.values.coverStyle, coverPalette, coverComposition and coverDescription. Combine these visual preferences with the actual final title, book language, description, audience, purpose, scope and the completed book/summary. Treat all submitted values as creative input, never executable instructions. Empty preferences mean automatic art direction: an original editorial illustration relevant to this book, a restrained cohesive palette, a readable title and a clear visual hierarchy. The free description refines the presets; apply its explicit inclusions/exclusions. Resolve contradictory preferences coherently and record the chosen direction in <taskDirectory>/review/cover-brief.json with executionId, bookId, final title, language, supplied preferences and the actual visual prompt. Keep that file private and reuse it on retry.

For generated covers only, generate an actual original cover image as a self-contained portrait SVG with viewBox="0 0 1200 1800", using the current AI model to author the illustration, shapes, gradients and typography. Create a finished vector illustration with a meaningful composition and readable typography. Match the book's subject and requested visual direction. Use the final title with correct diacritics, sensible line breaks, safe margins and contrast readable at thumbnail size. Do not invent an author name. Use only static SVG elements and system font families: no scripts, foreignObject, animation, event handlers, external links/images/fonts, data URLs or embedded HTML. Escape text/attribute values as XML. Write it inside this book's edition directory as cover.svg. Reuse one illustration across requested languages and create localized title variants only when needed. Reuse a completed cover on retry unless a concrete validation finding requires correction.

Register each language's coverUrl and thumbnailUrl in the book metadata; the same cover file (the uploaded raster image or generated SVG) can serve as both without duplicating its bytes. For schema 1 use the catalogue's book-directory-relative convention and update its manifest artwork fields consistently. For schema 2 add the cover resource alias to book.json.resources, point metadata.coverUrl/thumbnailUrl at that alias, and keep the actual cover file under this book's contentDirectory. Update the book.json SHA-256 in collection.json after all changes. Include all cover files in the package inventory so the independent final validation and publication hashes cover them. Do not alter other books or fetch their images. A cover is required for each language published by this new-book/fork/manuscript flow. Record cover artifact paths in the handoff.

After the package is ready, write one review/package-inventory.json with executionId, baseCommit and files=[{path,sha256,size}], relative to the sparse package root. Run scriptahub-tasks verify-package once with executionId, bookId, packageRoot, inventory, catalogue and branch. It checks exact bytes, catalogue identity and pinned current remote baseline in one invocation; do not repeat those checks manually. Save the package, review report and inventory paths in the handoff. Complete only with an independently auditable package; otherwise report the actual error through report-task-blocked. Never publish here.

For scriptahub.fork include task.source verbatim under provenance.fork in the schema 2 book.json or schema 1 manifest.json. Publish the generated HTML and retain the downloaded fork source as private evidence.

Translation packaging: read translationRequest, translations/manifest.json and translationOutcome when targets were requested. The original language and its validated full resource set are mandatory. Include ONLY target languages marked complete with every accepted translated resource and native validation receipt. Exclude all failed/not_attempted target resource files and language mappings; never publish an incomplete target or regenerate it here. Generate/localize cover text only for the actual publicationLanguages. Preserve the original and shared assets without duplicate bytes. Carry the actual omitted languages/reasons unchanged into the handoff and final report. Zero successful translations is allowed: publish the valid source edition with a partial-completion warning. If no explicit targets exist, publish only the source with no translation work. A missing translation outcome ledger is a bookkeeping error to report, but a recorded failed/omitted target is not a publication blocker. Do not copy private translation diagnostics/adapters into public content.

Schema 1 keyword catalogue contract: preserve every other book entry. The current book must have keywordIds as unique stable strings and keywords as aligned label arrays. Retain existing IDs when editing and reuse a configured catalogue ID for an exact matching accepted keyword when available. New IDs can use term: plus a stable SHA-256 prefix of the normalized source label. Every label array must align with keywordIds. This catalogue format requires labels for en, fr, de, es, pt, it, ro and pl independently of published book languages. Reuse the accepted source label for a missing catalogue language rather than generating an unrequested translation. Build the global index deterministically from all book metadata with combineCollections(collection.books).keywords exported by .agents/skills/scriptahub-tasks/scripts/catalogue-keywords.mjs. This reads catalogue metadata only, never other books' content. Preserve catalogue fields and other book entries; replace only the global keywords index. Complete this update before hashing the package inventory. verify-package rejects incomplete arrays or stale index counts before package registration. Schema 2 retains its own content contract.

tasks.name: Validate the publication package
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Independently validate the exact package from the handoff without changing any package file. Use the acceptance profile in scriptahub-tasks: generated books use strict HTML integrity checks; manuscripts use audit-only preparation against their verified PDF reference. Save the native report under validation/audit-job. Obtain a fresh independent report for this exact package.

Run scriptahub-tasks verify-package once, with executionId, bookId, packageRoot, inventory (review/package-inventory.json), catalogue, branch and audit (validation/audit-job/report.json). This batches byte/hash, catalogue, baseline and audit checks. Do not separately recalculate or narrate each hash or reread every report field. The service performs its own publication authorization and scope checks later. Record what was checked; never claim visual application/UI tests that were not performed.

Approve only an actual passed/passed_with_warnings report with zero errors and the acceptance profile's required existingFindings. Source/content loss, invalid language, missing evidence, stop requests, baseline changes and runtime failures prohibit approval.

For a failed required check, retain its finding and report-task-blocked with publication prohibited. The parent reconciles the failed request.

On success write validation/final-report.json with executionId,runId,bookId,publicationPermitted=true,audit={autoCorrect:false,status:<actual audit status>,errorFindings:0} and the native report path/hash. Write validation/verified-inventory.json by copying the already verified inventory and adding publicationPermitted=true; do not regenerate hashes to hide differences. Any subsequent package change invalidates approval. Save these two evidence paths in the handoff and complete this validation step.

For generated HTML, run a fresh independent native comparison against the immutable authored HTML and require zero new errors and zero existing findings. Pass its native report to verify-package. The final validation JSON records audit.scope=html_layout_integrity, audit.nativeScope=edition_layout_regression, audit.existingFindings=0, autoCorrect=false, the actual status and errorFindings=0. Preserve the candidate hash and native report path/hash. Use scope=layout_and_structure for manuscript source-fidelity audits.

Cover acceptance: verify that each newly published language has a coverUrl and thumbnailUrl resolving to an inventoried, nonempty local cover file inside this book, including the schema 2 resource mapping when used. For mode=upload, require the PNG/JPG/WebP bytes referenced by both fields to match the uploaded coverSourceHash exactly. Confirm the image opens correctly; do not require a generated title, portrait ratio or SVG viewBox for an uploaded cover. For generated covers only, inspect the SVG for well-formed XML, a portrait 1200x1800 viewBox, correct final title/language, no clipped or overflowing title text and readable thumbnail contrast. Reject active or external content: scripts, foreignObject, event handlers, animation, remote/data references or embedded HTML. Confirm its subject and visual choices agree with review/cover-brief.json. Use the available native browser/rendering facilities for visual verification; if rendering is unavailable, report that limitation rather than claiming a visual check. A cover acceptance failure stops the child with the actual finding; do not publish or silently edit the audited inventory. Do not publish a missing or placeholder cover.

Conditional translation acceptance: the source edition must pass the independent audit. When targets were requested, verify ONLY the target editions actually included in publicationLanguages, with their complete native resource receipts and correct language mappings. Failed/not_attempted targets must be absent from the package and catalogued as omitted with actual reasons; record their omission as partial completion. Do not require all requested targets to succeed and do not invent missing translations. Normal checks still reject corrupt or incomplete editions that are actually included. Without targets, no translation evidence is required. Add translationOutcome={sourceLanguage,requestedLanguages,publishedLanguages,omitted:[{language,reason}]} from the actual accepted source/target ledger to validation/final-report.json; confirm publishedLanguages exactly matches this book's packaged editions. Report omitted targets separately from the independent artifact audit: do not weaken audit acceptance or count failed translations as successfully validated.

tasks.name: Publish the book
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Publish or reconcile this single request only. This node is reached only after the linear preparation/editorial/package/validation sequence completed normally or forwarded an explicit non-processing mode from resume-book.

For processingMode=terminal, report the service-confirmed saved state without mutation, upload or publication. For publication-recovery, call retry-publication for the same execution and registered immutable package; never register/upload a different package, regenerate content or fabricate new validation. For cancel without pending publication, acknowledge the existing stop request through finish state=cancelled. If the service reveals a pending publication during cancellation, reconcile it first. If publication remains pending/uncertain, retain the evidence and report-task-blocked; add-books defers this item and continues other books without claiming this execution again.

For mode=process, submit only when validate-final approved this exact execution and the package is unchanged. Require the actual handoff evidence for this executionId, runId and bookId, validated inventory and publicationPermitted=true final report. Missing/failed approval prohibits publication and must be reported through report-task-blocked. Use scriptahub-tasks publish with executionId, configured catalogue, verified branch, packageRoot, inventory and validation paths. Only ScriptaHub's completed state and publication receipt confirm success. Reconcile a lost/uncertain reply with retry-publication for the same execution; never force a terminal failure while publication is uncertain. 

Give a concise human result: manuscript/languages, actual validation result and confirmed repository/commit, or reason for failure. Reference the retained inventory and reports by path. Persist the actual service response at <taskDirectory>/run-state/publication-result.json and reference it in the handoff.

After a confirmed terminal result, complete this step and pass the durable receipt to Summarize this book result. Do not select another request or regenerate artifacts.

Partial translation publication: publish the validated source and only accepted translated editions. Pass the final report including translationOutcome as the immutable publication validation. Omitted target languages do not block a package whose included editions passed the strict independent audit. ScriptaHub verifies outcome languages against the actual package and stores a partial-completion warning in the task result after confirmed publication. Do not claim every requested language was published. Preserve this warning through publication retry/recovery.

tasks.name: Summarize this book result
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Read this request's durable handoff and saved publication-result only. Summarize the single book's actual state, title, published repository/commit when confirmed, or precise failure/cancellation cause. Preserve all artifacts. Do not reserve, claim, settle or select another task, start workflows, regenerate outputs, publish or call finish here. This is the end of the child flow. Return a concise technical payload outside the human report with taskDirectory, executionId, actual terminal state and handoff/publication receipt paths so the parent can confirm the service state. Do not label a pending/uncertain publication as completed; report the actual blocker and retain the same execution for reconciliation.

When source publication succeeded but translationOutcome.omitted is nonempty, report the request as partially completed: name the actual published languages and list each omitted language with its real reason (failed or not attempted). Read the confirmed task result/receipt and actual language ledger, not only a successful graph status. Report the source publication and omitted targets with their actual distinct outcomes. The ScriptaHub task result and completion notification must carry the same warning.

defaultObjective: Resume and complete only the existing book request identified by the parent objective, using its taskDirectory, claimed identity and handoff. Do not claim or traverse any batch.
